_what_this_is: Ethereum addresses reached from GCR's own public claims, with the evidence
for each and an explicit confidence tier. This is the only part of the GCR
material that is FLOW rather than STYLE: every other check in
src/gcr_hypothesis.py compares trading habits and can at best nudge a prior,
whereas an address either transacts with the target or it does not.
NONE of these has ever touched Hyperliquid (checked 2026-09-10: all four HL
endpoints answered, all empty -- a real 'no', not a failed read). None is a
counterparty of the target. That is why they are a WATCHLIST and not a
finding: their value is entirely in the future, if one of them ever moves.
Rule 8 applies throughout: a transfer is not ownership. Only the 'confirmed'
tier is asserted as GCR's; everything below it is a lead.

The watch now covers ALL NINE cluster addresses, leads included, and asks the full endpoint surface rather than perp-state-and-fills. The tier travels with every hit so a human can weigh a lead differently from the confirmed wallet.

deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.question: Does ANY cluster address have a Hyperliquid account, on any part of the venue?
deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.answer: No. Zero of ten addresses shows real use.
deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.method: Ten addresses (the nine cluster members plus @TwoDollaHotDoge, the NFT buyer) against twelve endpoints each: clearinghouseState, spotClearinghouseState, userVaultEquities, subAccounts, extraAgents, openOrders, historicalOrders, userFills, userFunding, userNonFundingLedgerUpdates, userFees, referral. 120 calls, 0 unreadable — every one of these is an answer, not a failed read.
deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.why_the_wider_sweep: The earlier check asked only for perp state, fills and ledger. An account can exist without holding a perp position: spot-only, sitting in a vault, trading under a subaccount, or having authorised an agent and nothing else. None of those exists here — but the shallow check could not have seen them, so scripts/check_gcr_wallets.py now asks the wider set daily.
deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.result: Nine of ten return nothing on every endpoint. The tenth, 0x398d2824..., holds 2 spot balances, 1 fill and 3 ledger rows — all inbound, zero outbound, and the fill is an automatic Spot Dust Conversion. Airdrop spam, not use.
deep_hyperliquid_sweep_2026_09_10.no_subaccounts_no_agents: Worth stating separately: subAccounts and extraAgents are empty for every address. So no cluster address is the parent of a Hyperliquid subaccount, and none has authorised an agent — two ways a GCR address could have traded while looking idle itself.
two_measurement_traps_found_and_fixed: userFees ALWAYS returns a 16-entry dailyUserVlm array, and each entry's
`exchange` field is the WHOLE VENUE's daily volume. A naive measure flagged
all ten addresses as active, including @TwoDollaHotDoge. Only userCross and
userAdd belong to the account being asked about.
A fill with dir 'Spot Dust Conversion' is the venue sweeping worthless
balances automatically. Counting it as a trade marked 0x398d2824... as REAL
